claim: Cardiomyocyte β3-adrenoceptors (β3-ARs) coupled to soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC)-dependent production of cGMP have been shown to protect from heart failure.
source: Cardiomyocyte β3-adrenoceptors (β3-ARs) coupled to soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC)-dependent production of the second messenger 3',5'-cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) have been shown to protect from heart failure.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature establishing the protective role of β3-AR/cGMP signaling.

claim: The exact localization of β3-ARs to fine membrane structures and subcellular compartmentation of β3-AR/cGMP signals in health and disease remain elusive.
source: However, the exact localization of these receptors to fine membrane structures and subcellular compartmentation of β3-AR/cGMP signals underpinning this protection in health and disease remain elusive.
evidence: This statement acknowledges a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: Functional β3-ARs are mostly confined to the T-tubules of healthy rat cardiomyocytes.
source: Here, we used a Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET)-based cGMP biosensor combined with scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM) to show that functional β3-ARs are mostly confined to the T-tubules of healthy rat cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using FRET and SICM techniques as described in the manuscript.

claim: Heart failure causes a decrease of the cGMP levels generated by β3-ARs.
source: Heart failure, induced via myocardial infarction, causes a decrease of the cGMP levels generated by these receptors and a change of subcellular cGMP compartmentation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements comparing control and failing cardiomyocytes.

claim: Heart failure causes a change of subcellular cGMP compartmentation.
source: Heart failure, induced via myocardial infarction, causes a decrease of the cGMP levels generated by these receptors and a change of subcellular cGMP compartmentation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing altered localization of β3-AR responses in failing cells.

claim: Attenuated cGMP signals led to impaired phosphodiesterase two dependent negative cGMP-to-cAMP cross-talk.
source: Furthermore, attenuated cGMP signals led to impaired phosphodiesterase two dependent negative cGMP-to-cAMP cross-talk.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using cAMP biosensors and PDE2 inhibitors.

claim: Topographic and functional reorganization of the β3-AR/cGMP signalosome happens in heart failure.
source: In conclusion, topographic and functional reorganization of the β3-AR/cGMP signalosome happens in heart failure and should be considered when designing new therapies acting via this receptor.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: Functional β3-adrenergic receptors have been found in cardiomyocytes isolated from various species including humans and rodents.
source: Over the last two decades, functional β3-adrenergic receptors (β3-ARs) have been found and studied in cardiomyocytes isolated from various species including humans and rodents (Gauthier et al., 1998; Mongillo et al., 2006; Hammond and Balligand, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: β3-ARs have been reported to couple to both stimulatory (Gs) and inhibitory (Gi) proteins depending on the cell type.
source: Depending on the cell type (cardiomyocytes vs adipocytes or atrial vs ventricular myocytes), β3-ARs have been reported to couple to both stimulatory (Gs) and inhibitory (Gi) proteins and to regulate cardiac contractility.
evidence: This claim is based on prior literature describing β3-AR coupling mechanisms.

claim: In human and rodent ventricular myocardium, catecholamine binding to β3-ARs elicits negative inotropic and positive lusitropic effects by signalling via Gi and cGMP.
source: In human and rodent ventricular myocardium, catecholamine binding to β3-ARs elicits negative inotropic and positive lusitropic effects by signalling via Gi and the second messenger 3',5'-cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) (Gauthier et al., 1998; Mongillo et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The β3-AR is resistant to agonist-induced desensitization, unlike β1- and β2-AR.
source: Unlike β1- and β2-AR, the β3-AR is resistant to agonist-induced desensitization, (Liggett et al., 1993; Nantel et al., 1993)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: β3-AR expression is increased in heart failure as well as in sepsis and diabetic cardiomyopathy.
source: and its expression is increased in heart failure as well as in sepsis and diabetic cardiomyopathy (Amour et al., 2007; Moniotte et al., 2007; Moniotte et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: β3-AR/cGMP pools can attenuate excessive cardiotoxic β1-AR/cAMP signalling.
source: It was hypothesised that β3-AR/cGMP pools can attenuate excessive cardiotoxic β1-AR/cAMP signalling, as well as pathological cardiac hypertrophy and remodelling which takes place in cardiomyocytes during the progression towards heart failure (Mongillo et al., 2006; Hammond and Balligand, 2012; Takimoto et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is based on a hypothesis supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) has been detected in close proximity to β3-ARs in cardiomyocyte caveolae structures.
source: Endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS), has been detected in close proximity to β3-ARs in cardiomyocyte caveolae structures.
evidence: This claim is based on prior research findings.

claim: Caveolae are believed to provide discrete signalling domains necessary for the autonomic regulation of the heart.
source: The caveolae are believed to provide discrete signalling domains, necessary for the autonomic regulation of the heart (Feron et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: β3-AR/cGMP is most likely degraded by phosphodiesterases 2 and 5.
source: It has been shown indirectly that β3-AR/cGMP is most likely degraded by the phosphodiesterases 2 and 5 (Mongillo et al., 2006; Takimoto et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research that showed this indirectly.

claim: Overexpression of β3-AR in transgenic mice protects the heart from catecholamine-induced hypertrophy and remodelling via an eNOS/sGC/cGMP-dependent signalling pathway.
source: Recently, overexpression of β3-AR in transgenic mice has been shown to protect the heart from catecholamine-induced hypertrophy and remodelling via an eNOS/soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC)/cGMP-dependent signalling pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent research.

claim: β3-ARs localize together with eNOS in caveolae-enriched membrane fractions.
source: The same study showed localization of β3-ARs together with eNOS in caveolae-enriched membrane fractions, which had been separated via ultracentrifugation (Belge et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The sGC subunit α1 facilitates the NO dependent but Ca2+ independent effects of β3-AR.
source: Another mouse study identified the sGC subunit α1 as the facilitator of the NO dependent but Ca2+ independent effects of β3-AR using sGC α1 KO mice (Cawley et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research using knockout mice.

claim: The 'soluble' sGC has been shown to act in close association with β3-ARs and membrane located signalosomes.
source: Despite its name the 'soluble' sGC has been shown to act in close association with β3-ARs and membrane located signalosomes (Mongillo et al., 2006; Feron et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The exact localization of functional β3-ARs in adult cardiomyocytes and the spatio-temporal regulation of their cGMP signals have not been studied before.
source: However, the exact localization of functional β3-ARs in adult cardiomyocytes and the spatio-temporal regulation of their cGMP signals as well as their potential interaction with cAMP signalling pathways have not been studied before.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: The study employs a highly sensitive FRET-based biosensor, red cGES-DE5, in combination with SICM.
source: In this study, we employ a highly sensitive Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET)-based biosensor, red cGES-DE5, in combination with scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: In healthy rat cardiomyocytes, functional β3-ARs are localized exclusively within the transverse (T)-tubules.
source: We demonstrate that in healthy rat cardiomyocytes, functional β3-ARs are localized exclusively within the transverse (T)-tubules and stimulate a cGMP pool which is predominantly regulated by phosphodiesterases (PDEs) 2 and 5.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using SICM/FRET.

claim: β3-ARs stimulate a cGMP pool which is predominantly regulated by phosphodiesterases 2 and 5.
source: We demonstrate that in healthy rat cardiomyocytes, functional β3-ARs are localized exclusively within the transverse (T)-tubules and stimulate a cGMP pool which is predominantly regulated by phosphodiesterases (PDEs) 2 and 5.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using PDE inhibitors.

claim: β3-AR stimulation can decrease overall adenylate cyclase dependent cAMP levels in healthy cardiomyocytes by a PDE2-mediated cGMP-to-cAMP cross-talk.
source: Furthermore, by using the cAMP specific FRET-based biosensor Epac1-camps we show that β3-AR stimulation can decrease overall adenylate cyclase dependent cAMP levels in healthy cardiomyocytes by a PDE2-mediated cGMP-to-cAMP cross-talk.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using cAMP biosensors and PDE2 inhibitors.

claim: The cGMP-to-cAMP cross-talk appears to be disrupted in heart failure, where β3-AR stimulation no longer has a significant effect on overall cAMP levels.
source: This cross-talk appears to be disrupted in heart failure, where β3-AR stimulation no longer has a significant effect on overall cAMP levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing control and failing cardiomyocytes.

claim: In failing cells, β3-AR/cGMP signals decrease in the T-tubules.
source: In failing cells, β3-AR/cGMP signals decrease in the T-tubules.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using SICM/FRET in failing cardiomyocytes.

claim: Heart failure leads to altered co-localization of sGC and caveolin-3.
source: Heart failure leads to altered co-localization of sGC and caveolin-3, as shown via immunocytochemical staining.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from immunocytochemical staining.

claim: Alterations in heart failure result in the impairment of the β3-AR-dependent cGMP signalling pathway and of a PDE2-mediated β3-AR induced decrease of local cAMP.
source: Together, these alterations result in the impairment of the β3-AR-dependent cGMP signalling pathway and of a PDE2-mediated β3-AR induced decrease of local cAMP.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: Rats underwent left coronary artery ligation for 16 weeks as a model of heart failure.
source: As a model of heart failure, we used rats which underwent left coronary artery ligation for 16 weeks (Lyon et al., 2009).
evidence: This describes the experimental model used in the study.

claim: Data analysis showed typical clinical signs of heart failure, including a loss of pump function, left ventricular dilation and left ventricular wall thickening.
source: Data analysis showed typical clinical signs of heart failure, including a loss of pump function, left ventricular dilation and left ventricular wall thickening.
evidence: This claim is supported by echocardiographic and biometric data presented in Figure 1.

claim: β-adrenergic stimulation (ISO, 100 nmol/L) of healthy control rat ventricular cardiomyocytes led to the production of substantial amounts of cGMP in about 2/3 of all tested cells.
source: β-adrenergic stimulation (ISO, 100 nmol/L) of healthy control rat ventricular cardiomyocytes expressing the cGMP biosensor red cGES-DE5, led to the production of substantial amounts of cGMP (Figure 2A) in about 2/3 of all tested cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In failing cardiomyocytes, administration of ISO resulted in a significant two-fold reduction in the amount of detectable cGMP (p=0.0465).
source: In failing cardiomyocytes isolated from rats 16 weeks post-myocardial infarction, administration of the same saturating concentrations of ISO resulted in a significant two-fold reduction in the amount of detectable cGMP (Figure 2B, p=0.0465).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B with statistical significance.

claim: Blocking β1- and β2-ARs in control cells did not abolish cGMP production.
source: Blocking β1- and β2-ARs (with 100 nmol/L CGP20712A and 50 nmol/L ICI118551, respectively) in control cells did not abolish this cGMP production (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The cGMP signal was strongly and significantly inhibited in control cells by the application of the β3-AR antagonist SR59230A (p=0.0316).
source: The signal was however strongly and significantly inhibited in control cells by the application of the β3-AR antagonist SR59230A (Figure 2D, p=0.0316)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D with statistical significance.

claim: The cGMP signal was strongly and significantly inhibited by the nitric oxide synthase (NOS) blocker, L-NAME (p=0.0217).
source: or by the nitric oxide synthase (NOS) blocker, nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME, Figure 2E, p=0.0217).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E with statistical significance.

claim: β3-AR/cGMP levels are under the control of multiple PDEs.
source: We found that β3-AR/cGMP levels are under the control of multiple PDEs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using various PDE inhibitors.

claim: PDE1 inhibition has a minimal effect on β3-AR/cGMP production.
source: PDE1 inhibition has a minimal effect on β3-AR/cGMP production, whereas PDE2 and PDE5 represent the most prominent β3-AR/cGMP degrading families (Figure 3B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: PDE2 and PDE5 represent the most prominent β3-AR/cGMP degrading families.
source: PDE1 inhibition has a minimal effect on β3-AR/cGMP production, whereas PDE2 and PDE5 represent the most prominent β3-AR/cGMP degrading families (Figure 3B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Both PDE2 and PDE5 contribute to more than a half of the overall PDE inhibitory response as determined by IBMX treatment.
source: Both PDE2 and PDE5 contribute to more than a half of the overall PDE inhibitory response as determined by IBMX treatment (Figure 3B,D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In failing cells, the PDE2, PDE3 and PDE5 inhibitor effects showed a tendency towards increasing.
source: Furthermore, we observed that in failing cells, the PDE2, PDE3 and PDE5 inhibitor effects, while not statistically significant, showed a tendency towards increasing (Figure 3B,D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3, though not statistically significant.

claim: In healthy cardiomyocytes, functional β3-ARs reside mainly in the T-tubules with very few responses being detectable outside of T-tubules.
source: In healthy cardiomyocytes, we observed that functional β3-ARs reside mainly in the T-tubules with very few responses being detectable outside of T-tubules (Figure 4A–E)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using SICM/FRET shown in Figure 4.

claim: In failing cells, the β3-ARs responses after localized stimulation can be detected in both tubulated and non-tubulated areas across the sarcolemma.
source: whereas in failing cells, the β3-ARs responses after localized stimulation can be detected in both tubulated and non-tubulated areas across the sarcolemma (Figure 4F–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using SICM/FRET shown in Figure 4.

claim: The increased activity of β3-ARs in non-tubulated surface areas in failing cells might be linked to a disrupted association of β3-AR with caveolar signalosomes.
source: The increased activity of β3-ARs in non-tubulated surface areas in failing cells might be linked to a disrupted association of β3-AR with caveolar signalosomes.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: The T-tubular localization of the β3-AR can be abolished by treating cells with the TAT-C3SD peptide.
source: However, the T-tubular localization of the receptor can be abolished by treating cells with the TAT-C3SD peptide (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), so that the response level in the crest areas equals the response level of the T-tubules.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: sGCα1 partially co-localizes with caveolin-3.
source: We detected partial co-localization of sGCα1 with caveolin-3 (Figure 5A,C,E)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunocytochemical staining data shown in Figure 5.

claim: sGCα1 co-localization with caveolin-3 was significantly decreased by about 20% in failing cardiomyocytes (p=0.0014).
source: which was significantly decreased by about 20% in failing cardiomyocytes (Figure 5E, p=0.0014).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunocytochemical staining data shown in Figure 5E with statistical significance.

claim: sGCα1 co-localization with α-actinin had a tendency to increase in failing cardiomyocytes (p=0.0244).
source: Concomitantly, sGCα1 co-localization with the microfilament protein α-actinin (Figure 5B,D,F) had a tendency to increase in failing cardiomyocytes (Figure 5F, p=0.0244)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunocytochemical staining data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: sGCβ1 subunit co-localization with caveolin-3 decreased by about 16% (p=0.0044).
source: whereas sGCβ1 subunit co-localization with caveolin-3 also decreased by about 16% (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, p=0.0044), indicating a redistribution of sGC away from caveolin-rich microdomains.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunocytochemical staining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 with statistical significance.

claim: The decreased co-localization of sGC subunits with caveolin-3 indicates a redistribution of sGC away from caveolin-rich microdomains.
source: whereas sGCβ1 subunit co-localization with caveolin-3 also decreased by about 16% (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, p=0.0044), indicating a redistribution of sGC away from caveolin-rich microdomains.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-localization data.

claim: In healthy cells, stimulation of β3-AR led to a significant reduction of approximately 10.3% of the forskolin stimulated cAMP production (p=0.040).
source: In healthy cells, stimulation of β3-AR led to a significant reduction of approximately 10.3% of the forskolin stimulated cAMP production (Figure 6C, p=0.040).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using cAMP biosensors shown in Figure 6C with statistical significance.

claim: The PDE2 inhibitor BAY60-7550 was able to abolish the observed β3-AR agonist effects on cAMP levels (p=0.0458).
source: The PDE2 inhibitor BAY60-7550 used in this setting was able to abolish the observed β3-AR agonist effects on cAMP levels (Figure 6A,C, p=0.0458).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 with statistical significance.

claim: β3-ARs act via increased PDE2 activation to attenuate cAMP responses.
source: Nonetheless, our result suggests that β3-ARs acts via increased PDE2 activation to attenuate cAMP responses.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results with PDE2 inhibitors.

claim: In failing myocytes, the effect of CL316,243 on the cAMP response was no longer significant.
source: In failing myocytes, the effect of CL316,243 on the cAMP response was no longer significant (Figure 6B,C)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The PDE2 mediated cGMP-to-cAMP crosstalk is disrupted by disease.
source: suggesting that the PDE2 mediated cGMP-to-cAMP crosstalk is disrupted by disease.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results comparing control and failing cells.

claim: Previous studies have suggested that β3-ARs are localized in caveolae, in close proximity to eNOS and sGC.
source: Previous studies have suggested that the β3-AR are localized in caveolae, in close proximity to its signalling partners eNOS and sGC (Mongillo et al., 2006; Belge et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The exact sub-membrane localization of β3-AR and the compartmentation of its signalling to cGMP were not well understood.
source: However, the exact sub-membrane localization of β3-AR and the compartmentation of its signalling to cGMP were not well understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Alterations in β3-AR signalling in disease states have been difficult to study due to the lack of appropriate imaging techniques and specific antibodies.
source: Alterations in β3-AR signalling in disease states have been difficult to study due to the lack of appropriate imaging techniques and specific antibodies which work in situations of relatively low endogenous expression.
evidence: This statement explains the challenges in studying β3-AR signaling.

claim: In some, but not all cells, residual cGMP production was still detectable despite β3-AR and NOS inhibition.
source: In some, but not all cells, residual cGMP production was still detectable despite β3-AR and NOS inhibition. This is an observation which has previouslybeen reported in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes (Mongillo et al., 2006).
evidence: This observation is supported by experimental data and citation to prior research.

claim: β3-AR dependent cGMP pools are mainly formed in the T-tubules due to the localization of β3-ARs in close proximity to the caveolar signalosome.
source: β3-AR dependent cGMP pools are mainly formed in the T-tubules (see Figure 4C) due to the localization of β3-ARs in close proximity to the caveolar signalosome, which among other molecules is comprised of eNOS and sGC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and inference about the mechanism.

claim: The caveolar signalosome is comprised of eNOS and sGC among other molecules.
source: β3-AR dependent cGMP pools are mainly formed in the T-tubules (see Figure 4C) due to the localization of β3-ARs in close proximity to the caveolar signalosome, which among other molecules is comprised of eNOS and sGC.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about caveolar signalosomes.

claim: β3-AR-cGMP pools were induced outside of T-tubular domains when the caveolar signalosome was dissociated using TAT-C3SD peptide.
source: As a result, β3-AR-cGMP pools were induced outside of T-tubular domains (see Figure 4—figure supplement 1) which corroborates the importance of caveolar signalosomes for proper β3-AR regulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The dissociation of caveolar signalosomes corroborates the importance of caveolar signalosomes for proper β3-AR regulation.
source: As a result, β3-AR-cGMP pools were induced outside of T-tubular domains (see Figure 4—figure supplement 1) which corroborates the importance of caveolar signalosomes for proper β3-AR regulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results with the C3SD peptide.

claim: β3-AR/cGMP signals are similar to atrial natriuretic peptide-stimulated pools of submembrane cGMP in rat cardiomyocytes.
source: These findings are similar to what has been described for atrial natriuretic peptide-stimulated pools of submembrane cGMP in rat cardiomyocytes (Castro et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: β3-AR/cGMP signals are similar to eNOS/sGC-dependent pools of cGMP in mouse cells.
source: and eNOS/sGC-dependent pools of cGMP in mouse cells (Takimoto et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Further regulation via the cGMP specific and IBMX insensitive PDE9 cannot be completely excluded.
source: Further regulation via the cGMP specific and IBMX insensitive PDE9 cannot be completely excluded, although a recent study in mice suggests that PDE9 degrades cGMP pools generated downstream of natriuretic peptide receptors acting independently of NO (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculation based on prior research cited.

claim: The overall β3-AR/cGMP response was significantly reduced in failing cells despite increased β3-AR expression reported in cardiac disease.
source: Interestingly, the overall β3-AR/cGMP response was significantly reduced in failing cells (Figure 2B,F) despite increased β3-AR expression reported in cardiac disease (Hammond and Balligand, 2012; Moniotte et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and citations to prior research.

claim: The reduction in β3-AR/cGMP signal could be in part due to higher PDE activity on cGMP.
source: This reduction in the signal could be in part be due to higher PDE activity on cGMP (Figure 3B,E)
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The reduction in β3-AR/cGMP signal could be in part due to an altered subcellular arrangement of sGC.
source: and an altered subcellular arrangement of sGC (Figure 5).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Dysregulated caveolar signalosomes have been reported in a pressure overload induced heart failure model using mice.
source: Though the immunocytochemical method is limited in its spatial resolution and can therefore not resolve the caveolae structures themselves, it allows us to detect an alteration in sGC localization in heart failure, which could potentially be indicative of dysregulated caveolar signalosomes as reported previously in a pressure overload induced heart failure model using mice (Tsai et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Decreased expression of eNOS in the caveolae, alongside increased expression of neuronal NOS (nNOS) at the sarcoplasmic reticulum has been reported in studies of tissue from humans with heart failure.
source: Decreased expression of eNOS in the caveolae, alongside increased expression of neuronal NOS (nNOS) at the sarcoplasmic reticulum has been reported in studies of tissue from humans with heart failure (Damy et al., 2004; Drexler et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: eNOS function in cardiomyocytes has been shown to attenuate beta-adrenergic contractile responses.
source: As eNOS function in cardiomyocytes has been shown to attenuate beta-adrenergic contractile responses (Farah et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Potential changes in local NOS activities could contribute to altered β3-AR/cGMP signal disruption.
source: potential changes in local NOS activities for example due to decreased eNOS-caveolin-3 association (Feron et al., 1998) could further contribute to altered β3-AR/cGMP signal disruption.
evidence: This is a speculation based on prior research and the current findings.

claim: The slightly increased contributions of PDE2,3 and 5 to cGMP regulation in heart failure are probably responsible for the overall reduction in cGMP levels.
source: The slightly increased contributions of PDE2,3 and 5 to cGMP regulation which we observed in heart failure, are probably responsible for the overall reduction in cGMP levels, as can be seen when comparing total ISO plus IBMX responses in control and failing cells (Figures 2F and 3E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 2F and 3E.

claim: Increased expression and activity of the dual-specificity PDE2 has been shown in human heart failure.
source: Increased expression and activity of the dual-specificity PDE2 has been shown in human heart failure (Mehel et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: An increase in both cGMP and cAMP hydrolysis by PDE2 took place in a rodent model of aortic banding.
source: as well as in a rodent model of aortic banding, where an increase in both cGMP and cAMP hydrolysis took place (Yanaka et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: cGMP can increase the effect of PDE2 on cAMP by binding to the PDE's GAF-B domain and leading to a conformational change.
source: At the same time as being degraded by PDE2, cGMP can also increase the effect of PDE2 on cAMP by binding to the PDE's GAF-B domain and leading to a conformational change, thereby triggering the so-called cGMP-to-cAMP crosstalk.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about PDE2 mechanism.

claim: cAMP has increasingly been associated with detrimental signalling pathways in the context of heart failure.
source: This crosstalk between the second messengers of which one (cAMP) has increasingly been associated with detrimental signalling pathways in the context of heart failure, which the other (cGMP) could potentially attenuate (Mongillo et al., 2006; Moniotte et al., 2001; Yanaka et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: cGMP could potentially attenuate detrimental cAMP signalling pathways in heart failure.
source: This crosstalk between the second messengers of which one (cAMP) has increasingly been associated with detrimental signalling pathways in the context of heart failure, which the other (cGMP) could potentially attenuate (Mongillo et al., 2006; Moniotte et al., 2001; Yanaka et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The impairment of the cGMP/cAMP crosstalk supports the hypothesis of dramatic spatial rearrangements in the β3-AR/sGC/PDE2 signalosome.
source: This observed impairment of the cGMP/cAMP crosstalk further supports the hypothesis of dramatic spatial rearrangements in the β3-AR/sGC/PDE2 signalosome which impair cGMP dynamics
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: Spatial rearrangements in the β3-AR/sGC/PDE2 signalosome could potentially lead to depressed β3-AR effects on cardiac contractility demonstrated in similar animal models.
source: and could potentially lead to depressed β3-AR effects on cardiac contractility demonstrated in similar animal models (Mongillo et al., 2006) and in human heart tissue samples (Moniotte et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the current findings and citations to prior research.

claim: The observed response of β3-AR stimulation of about 10 percent on overall cAMP levels could be of physiological relevance when brought into the context of lowering pathological cAMP signalling levels.
source: The observed response of β3-AR stimulation of about 10 percent on overall cAMP levels, as measured via the cytosolic FRET sensor Epac1-camps, could be of physiological relevance when brought into the context of lowering pathological cAMP signalling levels on a whole or in confined signalling compartments.
evidence: This is an inference about the physiological significance of the experimental findings.

claim: Altered compartmentation of subcellular cGMP may play a role in disease-associated changes in β-AR signalling.
source: We believe that altered compartmentation of subcellular cGMP may play a role in disease-associated changes in β-AR signalling.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study findings.

claim: Heart failure does not completely ablate β3-AR/cGMP responses, leaving room for a residual cardioprotective action of β3-ARs in the failing heart.
source: However, heart failure does not completely ablate β3-AR/cGMP responses, leaving room for a residual cardioprotective action of β3-ARs in the failing heart.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing reduced but not absent responses.

claim: The therapeutic potential of β3-ARs is currently being addressed pharmacologically using the β3-AR agonist mirabegron in clinical studies to treat heart failure with preserved and reduced ejection fraction.
source: This therapeutic potential is currently being addressed pharmacologically using the β3-AR agonist mirabegron in clinical studies to treat heart failure with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (Pouleur et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a clinical study.

claim: The study reveals mechanisms of submembrane localization of cardiomyocyte β3-AR, which regulates the compartmentation of receptor coupling to cGMP production.
source: In summary, our study reveals mechanisms of submembrane localization of cardiomyocyte β3-AR, which regulates the compartmentation of receptor coupling to cGMP production and disease-driven alterations in β3-AR/cGMP signalling.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: The study reveals disease-driven alterations in β3-AR/cGMP signalling.
source: In summary, our study reveals mechanisms of submembrane localization of cardiomyocyte β3-AR, which regulates the compartmentation of receptor coupling to cGMP production and disease-driven alterations in β3-AR/cGMP signalling.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.
